messages:
maria docs: Hey team — I'm updating the Dedicated provisioning quickstart PR (#4127) to cover autoscale policy edge cases and isolation behavior. Draft is here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4127. Looking for content + SDK snippet help. PTAL.

alex: on it. which edge cases are you targeting?

maria docs: 1) tenant eviction ordering when reserved pool is exhausted
2) autoscale min/max with burst capacity interactions
3) SLA wording around burst vs committed capacity
4) example Terraform + Python SDK for creating a dedicated capacity and scale policy (and a short migration checklist).

jin: I can add the eviction diagram and a short paragraph clarifying preemption vs eviction semantics. Suggest we explicitly call out the "soft-preempt" behavior for workloads pinned with isolation decorators.

samir: for the SDK snippet — here's a minimal python example I use. It demonstrates create + wait + set autoscale policy:

```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
# create capacity
cap = client.create_capacity(name="qa-dedicated", gpu_type="a10", replicas=2)
# wait for READY
import time
for i in range(10):
    status = client.get_capacity(cap.id).status
    if status == "READY":
        break
    time.sleep(2 ** i)
# attach autoscale policy
client.set_autoscale_policy(cap.id, {
    "min_replicas": 2,
    "max_replicas": 8,
    "scale_up_cooldown": 60,
    "scale_down_cooldown": 120,
})
```

jin: nice. add a short comment about eventual consistency: create returns 202 and capacity may take a minute to become available.

leo: small nit — the link in the isolation section currently points to the old internal wiki. Need to fix to the public page: https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/isolation.

docs-bot: Link checker: found 1 broken link in the isolation section -> suggested replacement https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/isolation

maria docs: I updated the PR with jin's paragraph and samir's python snippet. Also added the Terraform example under /examples/dedicated/provisioning.tf and a short migration checklist for reserved pools -> dedicated. Can someone sanity-check the Terraform resource names and outputs?

alex: checking TF now. Quick note: autoscale policy example used `max_replicas: 0` in one spot — that's a bad default. Should be `max_replicas: 8`. Also call out the default cooldown of 60s in the docs.

samir: FYI the python SDK currently returns 202 for create requests; we should mention eventual consistency and show a simple backoff loop in the example (you did, thanks). Also suggest using the SDK helper `wait_for_capacity_ready(cap.id, timeout=600)` once we add that helper.

jin: suggested SLA sentence for the doc: "Dedicated SLAs cover uptime of the control plane and committed capacity; burst capacity is best-effort and subject to regional availability." We can shorten that to: "Committed capacity is SLA-backed; burst capacity is best-effort." Thoughts?

maria docs: pushed another commit with alex's fixes and added a wait loop per samir. Added a migration checklist with these steps: export reserved-pool config, map instance types to dedicated flavors, create dedicated capacity in staging, schedule migration window, cutover, monitor tails.

leo: LGTM after tests. QA — can you run through the quickstart and confirm the CLI sample works?

qa-bot: Ran quick check on linux docker image, CLI sample succeeded. Found one mismatch in arg name `--tenant` vs `--tenant-id` in the example; raised an issue in PR comments.

maria docs: thanks — fixed arg name and pushed. Anything else before merge?

alex: add a short code comment about `isolation_decorator` effects on preemption to cross-link to runtime docs (https://docs.redwood.ai/eng/runtime/preemption). Then merge.

samir: I can follow up with a short note to include in release notes to call out the example and migration checklist changes.

maria docs: Thanks all! Planning to merge tomorrow 09:00 PT if no blockers. :rocket:

(aside) maria docs: action items: alex - TF nit, jin - eviction diagram, samir - follow-up release note, leo - final QA pass, docs-bot - re-run link-checker after merge.
